In summary, we successfully synthesized the $\mathrm { ^ { 2 + } / ^ { 3 + } }$ codoped LRMO cathode material using a combined approach of co-precipitation and calcination approach.
This co-doping approach alleviated structural instability by suppressing changes in the O 2p band and reducing oxygen release during cycling.

Compared to pristine LRMO and single-element doped counterparts (Mg-LRMO and Al-LRMO), the co-doped Mg/Al-LRMO showcased significantly enhanced electrochemical performance, including excellent cycling stability (90.0% capacity retention after 200 cycles at 1.0C) and high rate performance (160.7mAh $\mathbf { g } ^ { - 1 }$ at 5.0C).
The co-doping strategy also suppressed the $\mathrm { O } ^ { 2 \mathrm { n - } }$ redox activity and minimized CEI film formation, further improving cycling stability.

This proposed codoping strategy could effectively address the challenges associated with LRMO cathode materials, providing a promising pathway for the development of high energy density and resilient cathode materials in the next-generation lithium-ion batteries.
